icons.heading: Accessibility
icons.description: Everyone is welcome. Strong: a deeper dip, a higher jump with the arms flung wider, a harder landing with two decaying bounces while the arms settle. The ring never moves.

icons.name: wheelchair-access
icons.heading: Wheelchair access
icons.description: The chair pushes off and goes. Light: the rider leans into a push, two speed lines stream out behind, and the chair pops a small wheelie back on its big wheel, then drops its front down with a hit and a small bounce; the head trails the chair by a beat. Strong: a harder push and a higher wheelie, a heavier landing with two decaying bounces. The chair stays rigid and ends exactly at rest; the speed lines are gone again.

icons.name: hearing-assistance
icons.heading: Hearing assistance
icons.description: Sound is carried into the ear. Light: the waves roll forward one step: the large arc travels on into the ear and fades as it arrives, the small arc swells into the large arc's place and a new small arc grows in from the source; the ear takes the arriving wave with a small hit and settles. Strong: two waves roll in, one after the other, and the ear takes two decaying hits. The waves end exactly where they started.

Strong: a deeper wind-up, the half snaps over to the inverted side and holds there a beat (light and dark swapped), then completes the turn, overshoots and settles. The ring never moves; the turn ends on the starting angle.

icons.name: reduced-motion
icons.heading: Reduced motion
icons.description: The ball brakes and its motion trails die down. Light: the ball lurches forward as it brakes and rocks back into place, while the three trails behind it retract to short stubs one after another, top to bottom, each snapping a little short and settling. Strong: the ball pumps the brakes twice, and the trails shrink in two steps, half way, then down to the stubs. The stubs hold; the reverse lets the trails stream out again.

icons.name: low-vision
icons.heading: Low vision
icons.description: A person who is blind or has low vision walks with a white cane and taps the way ahead. Light: the cane swings its tip up and forward, then taps down on the ground with a hit and a small rebound, and two tap marks flash out from the tip; the head nods a beat later. Strong: tap-tap: two sweeps and two taps, each with its marks, while the walker leans into the step and settles back. The walker and cane end exactly at rest; the marks are gone again.
